title: The borrowed rope
authoring_note: Original Cartesian Graphics prototype fiction inspired by the acts of hearing, remembering, interpreting and retelling. This is not an attested sakhi, historical testimony, sacred text, or a claim that living sakhi traditions are extinct. English development copy; no historical quotation or translation.

quartermaster_account.speaker: Quartermaster
quartermaster_account.text: I lent the spare lead-rope to a yard helper when the mare shied. It came back before evening. What I remember is someone keeping hold when letting go would have been easier.

trader_account.speaker: Market trader
lineage: Unnamed traveller, as reported by trader
trader_account.text: A traveller told me the helper took the household rope without asking. By the time the story reached my stall, the borrowed rope had become a stolen one. I saw neither the taking nor the return.

well_echo.speaker: Neighbour near the well
lineage: Unnamed traveller, as reported by trader
well_echo.text: The trader spoke of a helper taking a rope. That is where I heard it; I was not in the yard. Another voice repeating the tale does not make another witness.

quartermaster_reflection.speaker: Quartermaster, on remembering again
quartermaster_reflection.text: Now I remember the helper asking whether returning it would be enough. I said yes. Perhaps that is why I remember a loan. The traveller may remember a different moment. I can tell you what I said, not what every other person saw.

trace.text: A frayed length of rope hangs beside a repaired loop. You can see wear and a repair. Neither tells you who used it, when it was returned, or whether permission was given.
